extracted.intended_audience: researchers, authors, reviewers, readers, and platform operators who create, respond to, or interpret preprint feedback
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for creating, responding to, and interpreting feedback on preprints to improve quality, civility, and usefulness of public peer commentary. Applies to reviewers, authors, readers, and platforms that host or moderate preprint reviews and comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the content of the preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the content of the preprint
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Focused' theme. Emphasize substantive discussion of the manuscript's text, data, methods, and arguments rather than peripheral issues. These principles apply to preprint reviews on platforms such as Review Commons, eLife, ASAPbio Crowd, public comments on preprint servers, author responses, and reader interpretation. The overall aim is to elevate the quality, civility, and usefulness of preprint feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on science, not journal suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on science, not journal suitability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Focused' theme. Evaluate the scientific content, robustness, and clarity of the work rather than whether it is appropriate for a particular journal or editorial fit. Applicable across preprint-review platforms and public comments; intended to keep feedback relevant to the research itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on scientific rather than personal critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on scientific rather than personal critique
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Focused' theme. Avoid personal attacks, judgments about the authors, or commentary unrelated to the research; critiques should target claims, methods, and evidence. Helps maintain civility and constructive discourse in public feedback venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polish the tone to remain constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Polish the tone to remain constructive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Appropriate' theme. Frame critiques in a way that is helpful and actionable rather than hostile; use respectful language and consider how tone affects authors and readers. Applies to reviewers, commenters, and authors responding to feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect on possible biases in feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect on possible biases in feedback
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Appropriate' theme. Be aware of and disclose potential cognitive, social, or disciplinary biases that may shape interpretation or critique of the work. This self-reflection is intended to improve fairness and transparency in public preprint commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in scientific discourse responsibly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Appropriate' theme. Participate in discussions with a sense of responsibility for accuracy, clarity, and scientific norms; avoid spreading unverified claims or misrepresenting results. Applies to public reviewers, readers, and platform participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behave with integrity and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Appropriate' theme. Uphold ethical standards (e.g., avoid plagiarism, respect confidentiality where relevant) and act responsibly when providing or using preprint feedback. Intended to foster trustworthy public discourse around preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address inappropriate behavior when observed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Appropriate' theme. Take steps to call out or remediate abusive, biased, or unethical commentary—either directly or via platform reporting mechanisms—so that public feedback remains constructive and safe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make feedback useful with concrete details
rubrics_metrics.description: Make feedback useful with concrete details
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Specific' theme. Provide clear, actionable examples, references, or data points that explain the concern or suggestion rather than vague remarks. Concrete detail increases the usability of feedback for authors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate whether concerns are critical or optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether concerns are critical or optional
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Specific' theme. Distinguish between issues that fundamentally undermine the work and those that are suggestions for improvement or preferences, so authors can prioritize revisions appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether claims are supported by data
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether claims are supported by data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Specific' theme. Evaluate the match between claims and the evidence presented, including statistical support, methodological adequacy, and alternative explanations. Help authors and readers judge the strength of conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be candid about both strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Be candid about both strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Specific' theme. Provide balanced feedback that recognizes what the work does well in addition to areas needing improvement; candidness promotes fair and useful evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign feedback or provide attribution context
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign feedback or provide attribution context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Transparent' theme. When possible, identify yourself or explain your perspective/affiliation to give readers context for interpreting the feedback; anonymity or pseudonymity may be acceptable in some contexts but transparency aids credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge oversights when pointed out
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Transparent' theme. If errors or misunderstandings are identified in your feedback, promptly correct or retract them and be open about the change. This practice sustains trust in public review exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit all contributors to feedback
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the 'Transparent' theme. Recognize co-reviewers, collaborators, or others who contributed to the feedback so attribution is accurate and credit is given where due.
